questiontext.text:
Prove that \(2^n > n\) for every positive integer \(n\). Drag the blocks you need into the box, in order. Not every block belongs in the proof.

[[parsons input="ans1"]] {"steps": {# parsons_encode(proof_steps) #}, "headers": ["Your proof:"], "available_header": ["Drag from here:"]} [[/parsons]]
[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
A proof by induction has four parts: say what \(P(n)\) is, prove the base case, prove the induction step, and conclude. Here is one complete proof.

{@proof_display(ta, proof_steps)@}

The base case and the induction step do not depend on each other, so they may come in either order; only the conclusion needs both. Two blocks do not belong: assuming \(2^n > n\) for every \(n\) assumes what is to be proved, and checking \(n = 1, 2, 3\) does not prove the statement for every \(n\).

truefeedback.text: This is a complete proof. The base case and the induction step do not depend on each other, so either may come first; only the conclusion needs both.
The block ‘Assume that \(2^n > n\) for every positive integer \(n\)’ assumes what is to be proved, so the proof would be circular. The induction hypothesis assumes the statement for one value, \(k\).
Checking \(n = 1, 2\) and \(3\) does not prove the statement for every \(n\). The conclusion follows from the base case together with the induction step.
